info.description: Return the senders that have tried to use this account.
info.title: Mandrill

requests.description: Begins an export of your activity history. The activity will be exported to a zip archive containing a single file named activity.csv in the same format as you would be able to export from your account's activity view. It includes the following fields: Date, Email Address, Sender, Subject, Status, Tags, Opens, Clicks, Bounce Detail. If you have configured any custom metadata fields, they will be included in the exported data.
requests.name: POST /exports/activity.json

requests.description: Returns information about an export job. If the export job's state is 'complete', the returned data will include a URL you can use to fetch the results. Every export job produces a zip archive, but the format of the archive is distinct for each job type. The api calls that initiate exports include more details about the output format for that job type.
requests.name: POST /exports/info.json

requests.description: Returns a list of your exports.
requests.name: POST /exports/list.json

requests.description: Begins an export of your rejection blacklist. The blacklist will be exported to a zip archive containing a single file named rejects.csv that includes the following fields: email, reason, detail, created_at, expires_at, last_event_at, expires_at.
requests.name: POST /exports/rejects.json

requests.description: Begins an export of your rejection whitelist. The whitelist will be exported to a zip archive containing a single file named whitelist.csv that includes the following fields: email, detail, created_at.
requests.name: POST /exports/whitelist.json

requests.description: Add an inbound domain to your account
requests.name: POST /inbound/add-domain.json

requests.description: Add a new mailbox route to an inbound domain
requests.name: POST /inbound/add-route.json

requests.description: Check the MX settings for an inbound domain. The domain must have already been added with the add-domain call
requests.name: POST /inbound/check-domain.json

requests.description: Delete an inbound domain from the account. All mail will stop routing for this domain immediately.
requests.name: POST /inbound/delete-domain.json

requests.description: Delete an existing inbound mailbox route
requests.name: POST /inbound/delete-route.json

requests.description: List the domains that have been configured for inbound delivery
requests.name: POST /inbound/domains.json

requests.description: List the mailbox routes defined for an inbound domain
requests.name: POST /inbound/routes.json

requests.description: Take a raw MIME document destined for a domain with inbound domains set up, and send it to the inbound hook exactly as if it had been sent over SMTP
requests.name: POST /inbound/send-raw.json

requests.description: Update the pattern or webhook of an existing inbound mailbox route. If null is provided for any fields, the values will remain unchanged.
requests.name: POST /inbound/update-route.json

requests.description: Cancels the warmup process for a dedicated IP.
requests.name: POST /ips/cancel-warmup.json

requests.description: Tests whether a domain name is valid for use as the custom reverse DNS for a dedicated IP.
requests.name: POST /ips/check-custom-dns.json

requests.description: Creates a pool and returns it. If a pool already exists with this name, no action will be performed.
requests.name: POST /ips/create-pool.json

requests.description: Deletes a pool. A pool must be empty before you can delete it, and you cannot delete your default pool.
requests.name: POST /ips/delete-pool.json

requests.description: Deletes a dedicated IP. This is permanent and cannot be undone.
requests.name: POST /ips/delete.json

requests.description: Retrieves information about a single dedicated ip.
requests.name: POST /ips/info.json

requests.description: Lists your dedicated IP pools.
requests.name: POST /ips/list-pools.json

requests.description: Lists your dedicated IPs.
requests.name: POST /ips/list.json

requests.description: Describes a single dedicated IP pool.
requests.name: POST /ips/pool-info.json

requests.description: Requests an additional dedicated IP for your account. Accounts may have one outstanding request at any time, and provisioning requests are processed within 24 hours.
requests.name: POST /ips/provision.json

requests.description: Configures the custom DNS name for a dedicated IP.
requests.name: POST /ips/set-custom-dns.json

requests.description: Moves a dedicated IP to a different pool.
requests.name: POST /ips/set-pool.json

requests.description: Begins the warmup process for a dedicated IP. During the warmup process, Mandrill will gradually increase the percentage of your mail that is sent over the warming-up IP, over a period of roughly 30 days. The rest of your mail will be sent over shared IPs or other dedicated IPs in the same pool.
requests.name: POST /ips/start-warmup.json

requests.description: Cancels a scheduled email.
requests.name: POST /messages/cancel-scheduled.json

requests.description: Get the full content of a recently sent message
requests.name: POST /messages/content.json

requests.description: Get the information for a single recently sent message
requests.name: POST /messages/info.json

requests.description: Queries your scheduled emails by sender or recipient, or both.
requests.name: POST /messages/list-scheduled.json

requests.description: Parse the full MIME document for an email message, returning the content of the message broken into its constituent pieces
requests.name: POST /messages/parse.json

requests.description: Reschedules a scheduled email.
requests.name: POST /messages/reschedule.json

requests.description: Search the content of recently sent messages and return the aggregated hourly stats for matching messages
requests.name: POST /messages/search-time-series.json

requests.description: Search the content of recently sent messages and optionally narrow by date range, tags and senders. This method may be called up to 20 times per minute. If you need the data more often, you can use /messages/info.json to get the information for a single message, or webhooks to push activity to your own application for querying.
requests.name: POST /messages/search.json

requests.description: Take a raw MIME document for a message, and send it exactly as if it were sent through Mandrill's SMTP servers
requests.name: POST /messages/send-raw.json

requests.description: Send a new transactional message through Mandrill using a template
requests.name: POST /messages/send-template.json

requests.description: Send a new transactional message through Mandrill
requests.name: POST /messages/send.json

requests.description: Add a new custom metadata field to be indexed for the account.
requests.name: POST /metadata/add.json

requests.description: Delete an existing custom metadata field. Deletion isn't instataneous, and /metadata/list will continue to return the field until the asynchronous deletion process is complete.
requests.name: POST /metadata/delete.json

requests.description: Get the list of custom metadata fields indexed for the account.
requests.name: POST /metadata/list.json

requests.description: Update an existing custom metadata field.
requests.name: POST /metadata/update.json

requests.description: Adds an email to your email rejection blacklist. Addresses that you add manually will never expire and there is no reputation penalty for removing them from your blacklist. Attempting to blacklist an address that has been whitelisted will have no effect.
requests.name: POST /rejects/add.json

requests.description: Deletes an email rejection. There is no limit to how many rejections you can remove from your blacklist, but keep in mind that each deletion has an affect on your reputation.
requests.name: POST /rejects/delete.json

requests.description: Retrieves your email rejection blacklist. You can provide an email address to limit the results. Returns up to 1000 results. By default, entries that have expired are excluded from the results; set include_expired to true to include them.
requests.name: POST /rejects/list.json

requests.description: Adds a sender domain to your account. Sender domains are added automatically as you send, but you can use this call to add them ahead of time.
requests.name: POST /senders/add-domain.json

requests.description: Checks the SPF and DKIM settings for a domain. If you haven't already added this domain to your account, it will be added automatically.
requests.name: POST /senders/check-domain.json

requests.description: Returns the sender domains that have been added to this account.
requests.name: POST /senders/domains.json

requests.description: Return more detailed information about a single sender, including aggregates of recent stats
requests.name: POST /senders/info.json

requests.description: Return the senders that have tried to use this account.
requests.name: POST /senders/list.json
